q: Which goddess is said to have been born from the sea at Petra tou Romiou?
why: Legend says Aphrodite rose from the waves at this rock on the Paphos coast, which is why it's also called Aphrodite's Rock.

q: Which side of the road do you drive on in Cyprus?
o: Either, it depends on the town
why: Cyprus drives on the left, like the UK. Hire cars usually have red number plates so locals know to give you a little extra room.

q: Which plug will you need for your phone charger?
why: Cyprus uses the same three-pin sockets as the UK, so visitors from Britain don't need an adapter.

q: What currency do you pay with in Cyprus?
why: Cyprus switched from the Cypriot pound to the euro on 1 January 2008.

q: What number do you call in an emergency?
why: Both 112 and 199 reach the emergency services, free from any phone.

q: Halloumi is famous for doing what on the grill?
o: Holding its shape instead of melting
why: Halloumi has a high melting point, so it browns on the grill and squeaks when you bite it.

q: What is the highest mountain in Cyprus?
why: Mount Olympus in the Troodos range rises to 1,952 metres. In winter there's enough snow up there to ski.

q: Can you go skiing in Cyprus?
o: Yes, on Mount Olympus in winter
why: The Troodos mountains get snow most winters, and there are ski lifts on Mount Olympus.

q: Commandaria is one of the oldest named wines in the world. What kind of wine is it?
why: Commandaria is a sweet wine made from sun-dried grapes in villages on the slopes above Limassol.

q: How many painted churches in the Troodos mountains are on the UNESCO World Heritage list?
why: Ten churches and monasteries, many with simple barn-like roofs hiding remarkable painted interiors.

q: Choirokoitia, a UNESCO site between Larnaca and Limassol, is a village from which age?
o: The Neolithic, the late Stone Age
why: People lived in Choirokoitia's round stone houses around 9,000 years ago.

q: Kato Paphos Archaeological Park is best known for its…
why: The Roman villas at Kato Paphos have some of the finest floor mosaics in the Mediterranean.

q: At the Tombs of the Kings in Paphos, who was actually buried there?
o: Wealthy officials and aristocrats, not kings
why: The name comes from how grand the rock-cut tombs are. The people buried there were high-ranking officials and nobles.

q: Which Ayia Napa beach has a small island you can wade across to?
why: Nissi means island in Greek. On calm days you can walk across the sandbank to it.

q: How did Fig Tree Bay in Protaras get its name?
o: From a fig tree that has stood near the beach for centuries
From the fig farms that once covered the town
From a ship called The Fig Tree
From the shape of the bay
why: The bay is named after a fig tree said to have grown by the beach for centuries.

q: What is Cape Greco best known for?
o: Sea caves, cliffs and clear water
why: The headland between Ayia Napa and Protaras is a national forest park with sea caves and a natural rock arch.

q: Which birds turn Larnaca Salt Lake pink in winter?
why: Thousands of flamingos spend the winter on the lake, usually from around November to March.

q: Which saint is the famous church in the centre of Larnaca named after?
why: Tradition says Lazarus lived in Larnaca after leaving Bethany, and the church of Agios Lazaros stands over his tomb.

q: Lefkara village is famous for which handmade craft?
why: Lefkaritika lace is made by hand in the village. Legend has it Leonardo da Vinci bought a piece for Milan Cathedral.

q: Which animals come ashore to nest on the beaches of the Akamas, around Lara Bay?
why: Green and loggerhead turtles nest at Lara Bay in summer, and the beaches are protected for them.

q: Which wild sheep is the national animal of Cyprus?
why: The shy mouflon lives in the Paphos Forest, and you'll see it on Cypriot coins.

q: A Cypriot says “Kalimera!” as you arrive for breakfast. What does it mean?
why: Kalimera is good morning. Thank you is efcharistó, and cheers is yiamas.

q: Ordering a Cyprus coffee “metrio” gets you…
why: Sketo is no sugar, metrio is medium sweet and glykis is sweet.

q: What is kleftiko?
o: Lamb slow-cooked in a sealed oven
why: Kleftiko is lamb cooked slowly for hours, traditionally in a clay oven sealed with dough.

q: If you order a meze in a Cypriot taverna, what arrives?
o: Lots of small dishes, one after another
One big platter of grilled fish
why: A meze can run to 20 or more dishes, so pace yourself.

q: Cyprus is the Mediterranean's third largest island. Which two are bigger?
why: Only Sicily and Sardinia are bigger.

q: Kolossi Castle near Limassol was run by which order of knights?
o: The Knights of the Round Table
why: The Knights Hospitaller ran a large estate here, and Commandaria wine takes its name from their Grand Commandery.

q: What is the star sight at ancient Kourion, on the cliffs west of Limassol?
o: A Greco-Roman theatre overlooking the sea
why: The restored theatre still hosts summer concerts and plays, with the sea as the backdrop.
